source: Research/App Store Reviews/13. Productive - Habit Tracker - Daily Routine & Goals Planner/reviews.jsonl

record.title: It is what I’ve been looking for!
record.body:
Love this app! Has really helped me to stay on track and get things done! Love the Apple Watch app to easily touch the “complication” on the watch face that brings me to my list of activities for the morning/afternoon/ evening. Super helpful! Plus I love that you have the option to a start a timer right there for a selected activity (like reading for 30 mins). I used to tell myself I’ll sit and read for a large chunk of time, but wouldn’t get to it, so now I have it scheduled to read every morning and evening for 30 mins. The functionality and options within the app are well thought out and effective with minimization of tedious scheduling. The app is super encouraging as well! Just very well thought out. I’m glad I sprung for the membership deal when I signed up! Five stars.

————-

One suggestion or request I would make to the developers is the ability to add a Task (versus a habit) so that it is added easily to my “to do’s” 

(One thing I would like to understand is how things are sorted within the time of day. Sometimes I have to play with the details of the habit to make it appear in the order I want it to, so I’d like to know if there’s a trick to this - but usually it is intuitive!)

Thank you so much for creating this app!

source: Research/App Store Reviews/24. Fabulous - Daily Habit Tracker - Morning Routines & ADHD Help/reviews.jsonl

record.title: Immersive view is not great if you have ADHD
record.body:
I wanted to like Fabulous, because I really need routines in my day. I have ADHD and forming habits has been a life long struggle. 

The biggest issue is the immersive view. The idea behind it is great, but it is more cluttered and distracting than the list view. There’s a banner at the top encouraging me to take notes, a timer, music, artwork, sounds for everything, and like 3 banners at the bottom I couldn’t even process at that point. 

Secondly, the app keeps you from doing most things until you have read a lesson and answered a question about whether you agree. They also play cute videos at the end to tell you about your journey. Theoretically, that should improve your commitment to your goal. In practice, it acts as a distracting barrier to the routine. 

If I’m doing my morning or night routine, I’m already multitasking by using an app. I don’t need it demanding extra cognitive bandwidth on top of that. Fabulous is meant to support my routines, but more often than not, its design gets in the way.

source: Research/App Store Reviews/26. Eden - Daily Routine Planner - Self care habit tracker, to do/reviews.jsonl

record.title: A great and fun concept
record.body: Everyday you can create a checklist, up to 5 tasks before a membership is required. As you complete your list a flower will grow. On the contrary, an uncompleted task will wither or stunt the growth of the flower. I'm watering my digital plant by being productive, its instant dopamine boost seeing my flower healthy. No complaints so far except a few suggestions: Add a pause/save option on the timer. Currently you can either only pause the timer, which locks you onto the timer screen, or you quit which resets your timer. It'll be great for example, to set a goal of studying an hour a day, but allow the user to save 30min in and finish the task later. Have more plants! Right now its just a flower, add some other species and maybe even pets! It'll be great to see some overgrowth on my buttons if I'm on a streak :).

record.title: Widget Update Ruined the Tracking Flexibility
record.body: I used to love the old iOS home screen widget, where I could increment my habit progress one step at a time. For example, if I had to complete a habit twice a day, I could mark it once in the morning and once again later. Now, with the new widget, a single tap completes the entire habit, making it impossible to track partial progress throughout the day. This removes the flexibility and satisfaction of tracking habits gradually. Please bring back the old widget behavior or at least add an option to choose how the widget marks progress.

record.author: rheagoel96

source: Research/App Store Reviews/53. HabitMinder • Habit Tracker - Daily Reminders & Routines/reviews.jsonl

record.title: Outstanding - almost there
record.body:
Habit apps are a crowded marketplace, and this one really stands out to me. Gorgeous design that is very simple and easy on the eyes, but still very flexible. They found the right balance. It’s engaging and fun to check things off (might as well use the addictiveness of technology to help your productivity :) Their hydration app is equally fantastic. Both have earned a permanent spot in my “Today” view...assuming a few things are in the works. 

1. Mac app - visibility and management of tasks/habits is really only viable if you can access them (and synced notifications) from any device. 

2. The notification text is a bit odd. I wish these would just contain the habit text and nothing else. They often appear as verbose sentences that you have to read. For me this affects the fluidity of use. 

3. The Today widget could be enhanced by only showing remaining habits at the top. 

4. Ability both to skip habits or mark as failed would be nice. 

Items 2–4 are all ways of helping you see only what you need to see. The “at a glance” nature of this app isn’t quite there yet. 

The comments seem to indicate that more integration with multiple devices is forthcoming. Lack of this functionality is normally a dealbreaker for me, but I’m using this on my phone only for the moment because the app is just that good. At whatever point these become more integrated in the ecosystem, this and WaterMinder will unquestionably be 5 star software.

source: Research/App Store Reviews/56. Dots - Habit Tracker Widget - Daily Routine, Goal & Planner/reviews.jsonl

record.title: Exceptional, no nonsense app
record.body:
Sensational organisation app. The minimalism is absolutely perfect for people who actually want to track their habits without the faff. My ADHD makes organisation challenging and over the year I’ve tried countless apps that claim to help “neurodivergent people” or be “perfect for those who procrastinate.” They end up being made for quick cash grabs or having a wildly confusing interface that is overwhelming and challenging to navigate. 

With Dots, you get exactly what you download. All your habits trackable in a range of formats (card, list, calendar form) so you can check them off in the one you prefer. You can also add the widget to your home screen so you can cross habits off during the day without having to open the app. There’s no paywall, no ads, and it’s beautifully minimalistic. Everything I needed I am so thankful that I found this.
